checks.do: For a Connector that never registers after deployment, the cloud's provisioning inputs first: a provisioning template for that cloud and its URL in the deployment, an autoscaling template only for an autoscaling deployment, the credentials secret, and the instance identity's permissions to read it.

template-before-locations.title: Must the provisioning template be configured before locations?
template-before-locations.detail: The step-by-step guide puts the provisioning template (Step 2) before locations (Step 3), but the provisioning template form has a Location Template drop-down that is not marked optional. The captured pages do not say whether the template must come first or whether a Location Template must exist before the template is saved.

what-it-is.statement: Zscaler Cloud Connector is a virtual machine that simplifies traffic forwarding to Zscaler services, extending Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA) to cloud-native workloads.

quotes: Zscaler Cloud Connector is a virtual machine (VM) that simplifies traffic forwarding to Zscaler services. It extends the capabilities of Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA) to cloud-native workloads

internet-vs-private.statement: Internet & SaaS is used when a private workload communicates with a public workload through the Zero Trust Exchange; Private Access is used when two private workloads communicate with each other through it.

quotes: Internet & SaaS is used when a private workload is communicating to a public workload through the ZTE. Private Access is used when two private workloads are communicating with each other through the ZTE.

l4-controls.statement: Cloud Connector provides Layer 4 controls for east-west traffic, including subnet-to-subnet and VPC-to-VPC traffic across AWS, Azure and GCP, and for ingress traffic to public applications hosted there, with tag-based policies.

quotes: Cloud Connector provides Layer 4 security controls for east-west traffic, including subnet-to-subnet and virtual private cloud (VPC)-to-VPC communication across cloud providers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
Layer 4 controls are also used to secure ingress traffic for public applications hosted in AWS, Azure, and GCP.
the added flexibility of leveraging tag-based policies for Layer 4 controls.

config-step-order.statement: The Cloud Connector step-by-step guide orders configuration as: administrators and roles, provisioning template, locations, Cloud Connector VM deployment, firewall filtering, gateways, forwarding methods, then analytics.

quotes: - Step 1: Update Administrator and Role Management Information
- Step 2: Configure Your Provisioning Template
- Step 3: Configure Your Locations
- Step 4: Deploy Your Cloud Connector Virtual Machine (VM)
- Step 5: Configure Your Firewall Filtering
- Step 6: Configure Your Gateways
- Step 7: Configure Your Forwarding Methods
- Step 8: Configure Your Analytics

firewall-filtering-components.statement: The guide says firewall filtering policies are made of source IP groups, destination IP groups, IP pools and network services.

quotes: Firewall filtering policies are comprised of source IP groups, destination IP groups, IP pools, and network services.

provisioning-template-urls.statement: The guide says provisioning templates create the provisioning URLs used to deploy a Cloud Connector as a VM.

quotes: Provisioning templates create provisioning URLs to deploy your Cloud Connector as a virtual machine (VM).

reference-architecture-azure.statement: The Azure workloads reference architecture lists Cloud Connector as available as a virtual appliance in AWS and Microsoft Azure and as VMs for on-premises deployment, and that it enforces a security policy for cloud-to-cloud traffic; the Cloud Connector groups page says groups are created when deploying in AWS, Azure or GCP.

quotes: Cloud Connector groups are automatically created when you deploy a Zscaler Cloud Connector in Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
It is available as a virtual appliance in both Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure, as well as VMs for on-premises deployment.
Cloud Connector also enables multi-cloud connectivity and enforces a security policy for cloud-to-cloud traffic.

branch-connector-model.statement: The Branch Connector reference architecture says Branch Connector starts from a Zero Trust approach to the branch using the SASE model, leveraging ZIA and ZPA so users gain access to applications, not networks.

quotes: It starts with a Zero Trust approach to the branch office, using the Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) model.
Leveraging both Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), users gain access to applications, not networks.

onramps.statement: Cloud Connector is one of the ways to forward traffic to the Zero Trust Exchange, alongside Zscaler Client Connector, Branch Connector, and PAC files, GRE tunnels and IPSec tunnels (the last three for Internet & SaaS only).

quotes: Organizations can forward users, workload, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices to the ZTE using:
- Zscaler Client Connector - Cloud Connector - Branch Connector - PAC Files (Internet & SaaS only) - GRE Tunnels (Internet & SaaS only) - IPSec Tunnels (Internet & SaaS only)
